newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA COACHES SAY WINDIES MISSING BASICS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA COACHES SAY WINDIES MISSING BASICS.

text.p: Three Australian cricket coaches believe the struggling West Indies team is living in the past and that the former undisputed world champions should get back to basics, an Australian newspaper reported on Friday.
"They're living in the past," The Sydney Morning Herald quoted Queensland state coach John Buchanan as saying.

"A lot of the basics are missing from their approach...I've never seen a poorer fielding display than this team has given. There doesn't seem to be a concerted effort to restrict the basic indiscipline in the side," Buchanan said.

Buchanan also told the Herald he thought West Indies' practice of selecting four fast bowlers and one part-time spin bowler only worked in years gone by when the West Indians had four "top-class quicks".
Former Australia wicketkeeper and current Australian Cricket Academy coach Rod Marsh said all aspects of West Indies' fielding, from close catching to outfielding, needed work.
"They're not going to win too many one-day games fielding the way they are," Marsh said.
Former Australia pace bowler and current New South Wales state coach Geoff Lawson said the West Indians should work on their mental approach to the game.
"They should play a bit more selfishly," Lawson said. "By that I mean stop thinking about what people at home are saying and start playing for themselves."

West Indies were convincingly beaten in the first two tests of the current five-test series against Australia and also suffered heavy losses in their first two matches of the World Series limited overs tournament against the same opponents.
Star batsman Brian Lara has had a particularly disappointing series, failing to score a century so far and being disciplined after an incident during the second test in Sydney.
West Indies tour manager Clive Lloyd apologised to the Australia team after Lara stormed into the Australia dressing room to protest against his dismissal in that test.
Buchanan warned the poor performances and lack of discipline shown by West Indies would jeopardise the success of the tour.
"There are a lot of disappointed spectators and, I suppose, sponsors, out there at the moment," he said.
